regs_in_letter: FD&C Act misbranding (false or misleading); no CFR section cited in letter text

cases.claim: “. . . turn the page with VONJO” (VO, 0:04-0:07) | “. . . ask your doctor if it’s time to turn the page with VONJO” (VO, 0:51-0:54)
cases.context: Imagery of an elderly man walking his dog, eating ice cream, dancing; PERSIST-2 TSS coprimary endpoint failed vs best available therapy (p=0.08).
cases.rationale: Implies HRQoL/emotional/social functioning benefits not demonstrated; the symptom endpoint failed.
cases.check: Do taglines and lifestyle imagery imply quality-of-life or symptom benefits that the trials did not demonstrate (or that failed)?

cases.cat: Broadening of indication / omission of material indication information
cases.claim: The TV ad suggests the use of Vonjo in adults with certain types of MF and “low” platelet counts, without specifying what is considered “low.”
cases.rationale: Vague qualifier fails to communicate indicated population.
cases.check: Rule: flag vague population qualifiers ('low', 'certain', 'some') where the label specifies a numeric threshold or subtype.

cases.claim: Fails to communicate that bleeding can be severe, changes in electrical activity of the heart can be life-threatening, diarrhea is common and can also be severe, and increased risk of major cardiovascular events such as heart attack, stroke, or death.
cases.rationale: Omits severity qualifiers and MACE risk from PPI.
cases.check: Rule: compare each risk mention against PPI for severity words ('severe', 'life-threatening', 'death') and flag when dropped.

cases.claim: Major statement presented during pop-up book theme: pages turn, background music changes, dog barking and scaring ducks, ice cream cart, dancing with dog by a busker.
cases.rationale: Attention-grabbing visuals, frequent scene changes, and music interfere with comprehension.
cases.check: Are there scene changes, music changes, or engaging action during the major statement?
